title: Get Korea permission (K-ETA)
note:
Status (Nov 9): K-ETA account created, passport loaded. The Seoul dates are now fixed (land Mon Jan 11, leave Wed Jan 20); it still needs a Seoul address. Finish by about Dec 1.
Needed. Brazil is not one of the 22 countries exempt from the K-ETA (that exemption runs to Dec 31, 2026 and has never included Brazil).
Deadline: it must be approved before you board SIN → ICN (red-eye, 01:10 UTC+8 on Mon Jan 11). It usually takes up to 72h. Apply before leaving Brazil (by about Dec 1), because Gmail doesn't work in China without a VPN or roaming.
Cost KRW 10,000 + ~3% card fee (≈ US$7–8). Valid 3 years, multiple entries, up to 90 days per stay.
Needed: passport, face photo, email, card, and a Korean address (book a free-cancellation Seoul hostel and use that one). Update the address and dates on the site if they change.
With a K-ETA you don't need the e-Arrival card.
Apply ONLY at https://www.k-eta.go.kr or the official K-ETA app. Sites charging more are agents.

title: Check entry rules for each country
note:
China: visa-free 30 days per entry; the current policy runs to Dec 31, 2026.
Thailand: fill in the TDAC arrival card online before landing.
Singapore: visa-free for Brazilians (up to 30 days). Fill in the SG Arrival Card on the official ICA site (free) within 3 days before landing on Jan 10.
Korea: K-ETA (see above).
Japan: check the visa waiver for Brazilians is still in force.
Hong Kong: visa-free for Brazilians.

title: Set up Alipay / WeChat Pay
note: Link a foreign card before leaving. Most of China pays by QR code.

title: Install maps, translator and VPN apps
note: Amap or Apple Maps for China, a translator with offline Chinese, and a VPN set up before you land (Google, WhatsApp and Instagram are blocked in China).
